clue.text: The French bishop, one with relations who will behave badly?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who will behave badly'; the question mark flags the loose fit

blocks.note: RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A French bishop, surrounded by family who might misbehave at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hangs off the end: the whole charade is 'one', and the tail tells you what sort of one. A larrikin is Australian slang for a rowdy hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A larrikin is a boisterous, badly behaved person, especially in Australia.

clue.text: Put within confines of the law, girl is imprisoned in shelter

definitions.text: Put within confines of the law

indicators.note: what is imprisoned sits inside its jail

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A girl locked up in a refuge, with talk of legal limits: a shelter under the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imprisoned' and 'confines of the law' share a prison theme, but the law part is the definition and 'shelter' is LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To legalise something is to bring it within the law, making it lawful.

clue.text: Beginning to relax, old boy at home may be seen in the garden

definitions.text: may be seen in the garden
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for 'something that may be seen in the garden'

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A retired man starting to unwind at home, pottering in his garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The old boy relaxing at home sounds like the man in the garden; it is the bird. The robin is Britain's familiar garden bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a common garden bird, often seen following gardeners as they dig.

clue.text: Country responsible for taking control of wild animal

blocks.note: IC = in charge, i.e. responsible for, having taken control of
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A nation that has taken charge of managing its wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: IC, short for 'in charge', is a standard crossword abbreviation; the eland is a favourite crossword antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a country, the island nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Goddess is buried beneath island

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is beneath comes second

explanation.surface: A goddess lies entombed under an island, a myth in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'beneath' means 'after', so the island goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the chief goddess of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Sporty type who operates on the border?

definitions.text: Sporty type who operates on the border?

blocks.note: the surface reading: an athlete, here one who fights with a foil or sabre
the setter's second reading: someone who works along a field's edge, putting up the barriers there

explanation.walkthrough: The border clause steers you towards a smuggler or guard; the question mark flags a pun, since the swordsman and the man who puts up fences share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both kinds of fencer fit: the swordsman is a sporty type, the fence-builder works on boundaries.

clue.text: Longing to be given a new start to make an impression

indicators.text: to be given a new start
indicators.note: the word keeps its body but its first letter is replaced

blocks.note: itching = longing, eager; its I is swapped for E

explanation.surface: A yearning to begin again and make one's mark on the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an impression' reads as a whole phrase about impressing people; only 'an impression' is the definition, a print taken from an etched plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print, an impression taken from an etched metal plate.

clue.text: Instance in which right thunderous god appears as beast with pulling power

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A tale in which a thunder god turns into a strong animal, as in myth.
explanation.walkthrough: The shape-shifting god suggests a myth, but 'Instance' is the outer piece and 'appears as' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carthorse is a heavy horse bred for pulling carts.

clue.text: Live with uncontrollable desire

indicators.note: letters out of control run into a new order

explanation.surface: A life driven by passion one cannot rein in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live with' looks like a phrase, 'put up with'; 'Live' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to have one's home in a place.

clue.text: Beg Irish somehow to accept British nonsense

indicators.note: arranged somehow, in some other order

explanation.surface: A plea to the Irish to take in British nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BEG IRISH already looks nearly right; the British B goes in to double the first B.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean speech or writing that makes no sense.

clue.text: Transfer from hospital somewhere in Hampshire

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs
Andover is a town in Hampshire, a county in southern England

explanation.surface: A patient moved out of a hospital to another place in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfer from hospital' reads as one phrase about a patient; 'Transfer' alone is the definition and 'from' joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name the passing of power or duties from one party to another.

clue.text: Army unit and police crossing river

explanation.surface: Soldiers and police together crossing a river on a joint operation.
explanation.walkthrough: COPS goes around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military unit, larger than a division.

clue.text: Carriage light backed with gold

blocks.note: to light on something is to land on it, settle
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A carriage lamp mounted on a gold backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage light' reads as one noun, a coach lamp; split it. 'Light' is a verb, to settle, and 'backed' is not a reversal: the gold simply sits at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: A Parisian gets married — is husband trapped and unwanted?

indicators.note: what is trapped is held inside

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman marries; is the husband now stuck and unloved?
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Parisian' is the French word for 'a'; 'gets' just joins it to the married part.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something nobody hoped for is something nobody wants.

clue.text: Contentment of good boy brought before the head

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours or Sheerness

explanation.surface: The satisfaction of a well-behaved schoolboy sent before the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' looks like the headteacher; it is a head of land, a NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a state of quiet happiness.

clue.text: Man troubled with nag, scolder, gossip

indicators.note: troubled letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A man plagued by a nagging, scolding, gossiping partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The list of nag, scolder, gossip looks like three similar nouns; only the last is the definition, and the first two are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandalmonger spreads gossip; the noun gossip also means such a person.

clue.text: Disputations in AGM, unrest getting nasty

indicators.note: things that turn nasty get out of hand and messed about, so the order is thrown into disarray

blocks.note: the abbreviation taken letter for letter as part of the fodder
taken as written, the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: Rows break out at a company's annual general meeting as shareholder discontent turns ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGM is an annual general meeting of a company or club; its three letters join the six of 'unrest' to make the nine needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both plural nouns name heated quarrels or formal debates between opposing sides.

clue.text: Notice university with imposing exterior for one at ceremony there?

blocks.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A notice about a grand university building's façade, aimed at those attending a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' refers back to the university in the wordplay, a reuse the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduand is someone about to receive a degree at a graduation ceremony.

clue.text: Aristocrat using gardener here and there

indicators.note: letters scattered here and there end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A lord who employs a gardener to work round his estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here and there' sounds like the gardener's rounds; it is the anagram indicator, and 'using' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand seigneur is a great lord, a nobleman of high rank.

clue.text: Sailor without companions gets something to eat from the sea

definitions.text: something to eat from the sea

explanation.surface: A solitary sailor catches his dinner from the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible sea snail, a shellfish.

clue.text: Stupid people chat about ill-gotten gains

blocks.note: to gas is to chat idly

explanation.surface: Dim-witted crooks talking openly about their stolen money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the subject of', and it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in informal, chiefly American slang for awkward, foolish people.

clue.text: Vehicles getting hit, beginning to end

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the end

blocks.note: struck = hit; its S moves to the back

explanation.surface: Lorries being struck in a collision, front to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to end' is an instruction, not a description of the crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lorries are one kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Artist with a thousand things to read goes wild

blocks.note: M = a thousand, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A painter handed a thousand books loses control.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about wildly, to go wild.

clue.text: Cathedral precinct dean initially sealed off

blocks.note: a cathedral close is the enclosed grounds around it

explanation.surface: The dean has the cathedral grounds cordoned off.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral close is the precinct round a cathedral; the dean runs it, which makes the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a road or area that has been shut to the public.

clue.text: Woman in garden is upset? It’s a riddle

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: Eve lived in the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: A woman upset in the garden, and the reason is a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, but a riddle is also a coarse sieve for soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large coarse sieve, used for soil or gravel.

clue.text: Panel disagreed finally, with fuss ensuing

blocks.note: ado = fuss; 'ensuing' puts it after the D

explanation.surface: A committee panel finally splits, and a fuss follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panel' looks like a committee; it is a strip of wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower panelled part of an interior wall.

clue.text: Against having to travel on river

blocks.note: con = against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to be sent on a river journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travel on river' reads as a journey by boat; 'river' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is a great river of central Africa.

clue.text: Thus a father joins English gunners in series of programmes

explanation.surface: A dad signs up with English artillerymen, as in a TV drama.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the usual crossword gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama, a series of programmes.

clue.text: Scheme, say, lacking a supportive section

blocks.note: the A taken out of SAY
a stem is the part of a plant that holds it up

explanation.surface: A plan, for example, missing a structural part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', flagging Scheme as an example; it is taken literally as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean an organised plan or method.

clue.text: Big cask that may be on display in butcher’s window?

definitions.text: that may be on display in butcher’s window?
definitions.note: a descriptive clause for a thing, read as 'hog's head'

blocks.note: a large barrel, also a measure of beer or wine

blocks.clueFragment: that may be on display in butcher’s window?
blocks.note: read the answer as two words: a pig's head, shown among the meat

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: split the answer as HOG'S HEAD, a pig's head a butcher might show.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask, holding about 54 gallons.
